subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@astrahealth.com>, Claire Li <claire.li@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs

Hi Sam / Claire —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of what you shared (pain points)
- Cost: Current spend on OpenAI/Anthropic for embeddings + generation is unpredictable and rising with volume.
- Performance: Some latency spikes during peak hours for patient-facing flows (target p95 < 300ms).
- Data controls: Need to ensure PHI is never stored by third-party providers; must run in a private VPC or on-prem for sensitive models.
- Model drift / quality: You want predictable behavior and guardrails across prompt templates and rollout.

Current stack
- Production: OpenAI for chat/generation (gpt-4/4o) and embeddings, Anthropic for some summarization endpoints.
- Orchestration: In-house service routes to providers via a thin abstraction layer.
- Infra: GCP (us-west1) with a small fleet of inference VMs; data in BigQuery and Cloud Storage.

Success criteria for migration (what matters)
1) Quality parity or better on key prompts (triage, discharge summary, patient note condense) — measured by evaluation harness.
2) Latency: p95 generation < 300ms for 512-token context in peak load.
3) Cost: reduce per-token unit cost by 30–50% at 6M monthly prompt tokens.
4) Compliance: ability to run private deployment (VPC or on-prem) and KMS integration for keys.
5) Operational: same API surface for dev teams and observability into token-level costs.

Compatibility / constraints
- Must support standard OpenAI-compatible REST calls or a short adapter layer.
- Need models that can be quantized to int8/4 without catastrophic quality loss.
- Should work on NVIDIA A100 / T4 (your current infra).

Model shortlist (initial)
- Llama 2 (70B) family — good community tooling, quantization paths.
- Falcon (40B) — latency-friendly for some tasks, strong on structured generation.
- Mistral Inference variants (mix of sizes) — promising quality-to-cost.
- RedPajama / OpenAssistant fine-tuned options — for custom instruction tuning later.

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood to run a short eval (we’ll run 5–10 core prompts across candidate models + your gold outputs).
2) Security checklist: you to share the SOC2 / compliance questions (we flagged the most sensitive items in the attached PDF).
3) Technical deep-dive: schedule a session with your infra team to review VPC/on-prem packaging and quantization approaches (suggested: week of Mar 8).
4) Price/POC discussion: once eval looks good we’ll propose a Dedicated/Private sizing and cost estimate.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short XLS with extracted pain points and the security summary we discussed.

Thanks — I’ll circle back with proposed eval plan and sample prompts tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@astrahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Li <claire.li@astrahealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T09:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs

Marissa — thanks for the clean recap. This looks right. A few clarifications / items: 

- On latency: 300ms is our target for interactive flows. For batch summarization we can accept higher latency (p95 < 2s).
- On models: Llama 2 70B is on our shortlist but we’re worried about inference cost; please include quantized variants in the eval.
- Data residency: for the first phase we can use a private VPC deployment in GCP; on-prem might be required for certain cohorts later.

I attached our internal prompt set (sanitized) and a sample of your gold outputs for the triage flow — feel free to use them in the eval.

Next steps from our side: Claire will coordinate times for the infra deep-dive; we’re available Mar 9–11 PST.

Thanks — looking forward to the eval results.
—Sam
Director of Product, AI Platforms | Astra Health
sam.turner@astrahealth.com | +1 206-555-0108

Attachments: astra_prompt_set_sanitized.json, sample_gold_outputs.json
\

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-04T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Astra Health eval ask and owner assignment

Rishi / Aditya — looping you both in after Sam’s confirmation. Quick asks: 

1) Rishi — please own the eval run. Goal: run Llama2-70B (fp16), Llama2-70B-llama.cpp-int8 (or equivalent quant), Falcon-40B, and Mistral-7B-v0 on our reference infra. Use the sanitized prompt set Sam shared. Produce the evaluation report with: quality (ROUGE/BERTScore + human checks), latency (p50/p95 for 512-token context), and cost estimate at 6M tokens/month. Quote timeline: 5 business days for first pass.

2) Aditya — prep a short VPC deployment checklist and confirm KMS options for customer-managed keys. Also surface any blockers for A100 vs T4 execution and recommended instance sizing.

3) I’ll coordinate the Mar 9 infra deep-dive and own the proposal/POC pricing draft.

We should sync EOD Friday to confirm the evaluation plan and deliverables.

Cheers,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
